title: Background sync: what Android and iOS allow, and what they kill

videos.script:
Everything so far ran while the app was open. Today the planner syncs when it is not. {{asleep}} The phone is in a pocket, the screen is dark, and the outbox still holds three edits.

The app cannot just set a timer. {{ask}} It asks, and the system decides when, for how long, and whether at all. Android has Doze and standby buckets. iOS gives a refresh about thirty seconds, when it chooses to.

You read how each platform asks. {{three}} WorkManager on Android. BGTaskScheduler on iOS. Expo's background task in React Native, which sits on top of the other two.

All three end in the same place. {{stop}} The system can stop the sync at any moment, without warning.

So you write a sync that can be stopped. {{runs}} One step at a time, saved after each. You run it four times, kill it in the middle once, and watch the next run pick up exactly where it fell.
